paragraphs: Baker, here's what I think Jesus is teaching in this passage: you can stop being afraid of people. He tells His disciples, "So do not be afraid of them," and then He gives reasons, one after another (Matthew 10:26). Nothing hidden stays hidden, and what He whispers to them they get to proclaim from the housetops (Matthew 10:26-27). Two sparrows sell for a penny, yet not one falls "apart from the will of your Father," and Jesus says, "you are worth more than many sparrows" (Matthew 10:29, 31). I used to flinch at every rattle in that junk drawer, so trust me, hearing that you're seen and valued by the Father is the best news for a nervous heart.

But Jesus doesn't promise an easy road, and neither will I. He says He did not come to bring peace but a sword, and He says anyone who loves family more than Him, or who does not take up his cross and follow Him, is not worthy of Him (Matthew 10:34, 37-38). That is heavy, and I think it's meant to be. Jesus is asking for first place, because He says, "whoever loses his life for My sake will find it" (Matthew 10:39). Confessing Him before people is how you hold that place, and He promises to confess you before His Father in heaven (Matthew 10:32).

And here's the part that makes me grin, baker: following Jesus is also how you get welcomed and how you welcome others. Jesus says, "He who receives you receives Me, and he who receives Me receives the One who sent Me" (Matthew 10:40). Even "a cup of cold water" given to one of His disciples, and Jesus says that person "will never lose his reward" (Matthew 10:42). So no act is too small for Him to notice, and no fear is too big to hand over. Jesus then goes on to teach and preach in their cities (Matthew 11:1), and this story isn't over, so keep your oven warm.
